articles.title: Compare route difficulty grades between walking publishers
articles.summary: Read each publisher's grade criteria instead of treating route colours as universal.

sections.title: Find the grading key
paragraphs: A label such as easy or moderate has no single universal meaning across walking publishers. Read the specific publisher's explanation and note whether distance, ascent, surface and navigation are included.
Record the publisher and edition so a saved rating is not detached from its original context.

sections.title: Compare measurable details
paragraphs: Write down the stated route length, ascent and described surfaces separately from the overall grade. These details make two guides easier to compare.
Estimated walking time is not a guarantee; conditions and individual needs can make a route take longer.

sections.title: Record uncertainty
paragraphs: Mark missing information as unknown rather than assuming the route is accessible or straightforward.
Offline grades cannot confirm current closures or hazards. Choose a familiar alternative if important details remain unclear.

articles.title: Name exported offline maps so different editions stay distinct
articles.summary: Keep personal map exports findable without confusing download dates with source editions.

sections.title: Identify the region
paragraphs: Give each saved file a concise region label and add an edition only when the source actually supplies one.
A recent download does not prove the underlying path information is current.

sections.title: Distinguish versions
paragraphs: Keep an original separate from any annotated or cropped personal copy. Mark modified copies clearly.
Avoid including private home locations or personal journey details in filenames that might be shared.

sections.title: Test the file
paragraphs: Open the export without connectivity on a familiar location and check that the intended area appears.
A file stored on the phone may still require a compatible reader; keep an independent navigation reference.

articles.title: Keep a compact offline index of outdoor equipment manuals
articles.summary: Make model-specific care instructions retrievable without confusing similar products.

sections.title: Record the model
paragraphs: Write down the maker and exact model or variant printed on the item. Similar-looking equipment may have different materials and limits.
Keep sensitive serial numbers out of shared inventories unless there is a specific reason to disclose them.

sections.title: Save appropriate guidance
paragraphs: Store a permitted personal copy of manufacturer care instructions or an offline index pointing to the relevant section.
Generic checklists do not replace maker requirements for safety-critical equipment or specialist inspection.

sections.title: Maintain the index
paragraphs: Update records when an item is replaced, and label outdated instructions so they cannot be mistaken for current ones.
Test that saved files open in airplane mode; a web bookmark alone is not an offline manual.

articles.title: Organise a reusable pouch for ordinary dry litter on walks
articles.summary: Contain small packaging waste without mixing it with clean equipment.

sections.title: Choose the pouch
paragraphs: Use a washable pouch or small reused bag with a reliable closure for ordinary dry wrappers.
Keep it separate from food and drinking-water openings; this is not a container for sharp or hazardous waste.

sections.title: Carry responsibly
paragraphs: Place the pouch where it can be reached at a routine stop without obstructing movement or catching on branches.
Do not collect unidentified sharp objects or potentially contaminated waste from other people.

sections.title: Empty and maintain
paragraphs: Use an appropriate bin or carry ordinary litter home when no suitable bin is available.
Clean and dry reusable material according to its care instructions, and replace damaged closures.
